primaryCommitChecks.message: fix(validators): restore rendered rechecks and the 5% sample

feat(corpus): GET /corpus/pay estimates each active job's pay per token

A public, read-only route for miners choosing where to put their GPUs. Per
active period job: cap, price ceiling, tokens to saturate, the current
period's projection (min(cap, price x tokens verified so far) per million
tokens, dated by arrival as settlement dates them), periods ended but not
settled, the last 12 settled periods from their archives, the settlement lag
(oldest undecided submission) and prompts open. Header: current period, the
miners' alpha per period (chain, else the one frozen with a price) and the
subnet pool's alpha price in TAO (null when the chain is unreadable).

Cost: one recompute per 60 s whatever the request rate; the chain is read
every 10 min on its own thread and loop; archives are listed per task prefix
every 10 min on the storage listing loop and each read once. The settler
counts its unsettled verdicts by period on each pass (no new read); a split
judge exposes that count and the undecided age in its stats. Settlement and
weights are unchanged.

fix(validators): no checks or weights while ScrapingDog refuses the key or has no credits, no verdict on a task it refused, no JS rendering, 20 sampled pages per task

feat(corpus): a period pays at most a price per verified token

A period task may carry a price ceiling: each period pays
min(cap, price x its verified tokens), split by tokens, and the rest is
never paid. The budget bounds the whole period across settlement passes
(pay per period is kept in the settlement state). The archive holds the
reduced amounts, so weight setters pay it unchanged; a task without a
price settles exactly as before.

fix(corpus): export only finished completions, grade the answer after </think>

A completion that passed TOPLOC was exported whatever its ending: one cut at
max_new_tokens inside a thinking block was kept, and graded right when the
reasoning held the reference in a box (8.8% of hard-math completions).

Before any grading, a completion must end on the job's EOS and, in a thinking
render (chat-template-thinking-v1), close the block exactly once. Left-out
completions are counted by reason (unfinished_no_eos, unclosed_think,
multiple_think_close) in the delivery report counts, in export_rows' counts
and in the `jobs export` sidecar. The job filter now grades the text after
</think> in a thinking render, so a box or a code block left in the reasoning
no longer passes a wrong final answer.

feat(corpus): deduplicate a delivery's completions, within it and across jobs

v2 jobs run on the same prompts as their v1 (hard-math, science), so a miner
may resubmit to v2 a completion already submitted to v1. `dedupe` delivers a
completion once (fingerprint: sha256 of its token ids, else of its text), the
first copy in verdict-id order; `dedupe_against` (implies `dedupe`) also
leaves out every completion already in a passing submission of the named
jobs. Applied after the finished check and before grading; counted as
`duplicate_completion` (None when off), and the report gains a `dedupe` block.

Exposed as export_delivery(dedupe=, dedupe_against=), the admin delivery body
fields `dedupe`/`dedupe_against` (in scope, known, not the job itself) and
`jobs export --dedupe/--dedupe-against JOB`.

Test that every launched provider keeps the retained ACK bound

connect 1abca801 ("Bound retained provider returns to a silent
destination") bounds a provider's retained socket-owned returns with
SendBufferSettings.RetainedAckTimeout, default 240s. A provider fleet
operator reported on 2026-10-10 that providers kept their uplinks full
during the Main outages: retained TCP returns to destinations that never
answered were rewritten every MaxResendInterval until the process
restarted, and a swarm host did that for every provider it runs.

The zero value keeps that unbounded retention. The miner takes its
device settings from sdk.DefaultDeviceLocalSettings and changes no send
settings, so nothing here changes. This test holds it for the standalone
provider (ProviderDeviceSettings) and for a swarm member
(swarmMemberDeviceSettings).

The test needs the sibling ../connect checkout to contain 1abca801, so
merge connect's fix/bound-retained-return-retransmission first.
